deep.reconstruction:
Context: these are preparation notes for Grothendieck's late-1967 IHES lectures, published as 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (notes by Coates and Jussila, in Dix exposés sur la cohomologie des schémas, 1968). The page continues a computation of the cohomology of the infinitesimal (or stratifying) site of X/S, X formally smooth, using the formal completions X̃^{(ν+1)} of X in X^{ν+1}. Formally smooth means these completions cover the final object of the topos.

On the previous page X was affine and the F_{Δ^{(ν)}(i)} were quasi-coherent and Mittag-Leffler. This gave H^q(X̃^{(ν+1)}, F) = 0 for q>0, so H^*(X_inf, F) is the cohomology of the cosimplicial group ν ↦ lim_i F(Δ^{(ν)}_X(i)). This is a Čech–Alexander complex built from the formal neighbourhoods of the diagonals.

Here X need no longer be affine. For each ν, U ↦ F(U^{(ν+1)}/U) = lim_i F(Δ^{(ν)}_U(i)) is a sheaf F^{(ν)} on X_zar. As ν varies these form a cosimplicial sheaf F^*. Grothendieck claims two things:
- an isomorphism H^*(X_inf, F) ≅ ℍ^*(X_zar, F^*), the hypercohomology of the associated complex;
- hence the hypercohomology spectral sequence E_2^{pq} = H^p(ν ↦ H^q(X_zar, F^{(ν)})) ⇒ H^{p+q}(X_inf, F), which reduces to the affine isomorphism.

When F = O this is the Zariski hypercohomology of the completed Čech–Alexander complex. Via the cosimplicial-to-de Rham comparison it becomes the de Rham hypercohomology of X/S. A crossed-out passage started to specialise to F = O.

Section 6, 'Coh. cristalline': in char p (crystalline site), or when X is not formally smooth over S, X̃ no longer covers the final object. Instead one assumes an S-immersion X ↪ Y with Y formally smooth over S. The next page uses the formal neighbourhoods of X in Y^{ν+1}, and later their divided-power envelopes, to obtain the analogous Čech–Alexander spectral sequence for crystalline cohomology.
errors: No real error. The spectral sequence as written uses E_2 = H^p of the cosimplicial groups H^q(X_zar, F^{(ν)}). This is correct; it is the E_2 page of the first hypercohomology spectral sequence, whose E_1 is H^q(X_zar, F^{(p)}).

The isomorphism H^*(X_inf, F) ≅ ℍ^*(X_zar, F^*) tacitly uses the Mittag-Leffler / quasi-coherence hypotheses on every affine open, so that each F^{(ν)} computes Rπ_* locally. This is stated only implicitly (via the previous page).
In the crystalline (char p) setting the formal neighbourhoods in Y must be replaced by divided-power envelopes. Not yet said here, but done in the published lectures.

ideas.what: Cohomology of the infinitesimal/stratifying site of a formally smooth X computed via the cosimplicial system of formal completions of diagonals (Čech–Alexander complex)
ideas.modern_name: Čech–Alexander complex / infinitesimal cohomology = de Rham cohomology
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Crystals and de Rham cohomology of schemes, 1968)
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes, Dix exposés (1968), §§4-5

ideas.what: Globalization via a cosimplicial sheaf on X_zar and the hypercohomology spectral sequence
ideas.modern_name: hypercohomology of a cosimplicial sheaf / Čech–Alexander spectral sequence

ideas.what: For non-smooth X, or in char p, embed X into a formally smooth Y and use neighbourhoods of X in Y^{ν+1}
ideas.modern_name: computation of crystalline cohomology via embedding into smooth scheme (Čech–Alexander, PD-envelopes)

deep.surprise_reason: Draft of material that appears in the published 1968 Crystals lectures and in Berthelot's work. Nothing new beyond the order of exposition.
transcription_corrections: The first displayed isomorphism in the image reads H^*(X_{strat}, F) with the subscript partly overwritten (or X_inf?). The boxed spectral sequence has H^*(X_{inf}, F) (subscript hard to read).
Before ν in the boxed E_2 a crossed-out symbol is present; the rest reads E_2^{pq} = H^p(ν ↦ H^q(X_zar, F^{(ν)})).
The crossed-out passage reads approximately: 'Regardons le complexe F*, prenons pour simplifier F = O_{X_strat}', with a hatched box.

Section 6 reads approximately: 'Lorsqu'on travaille en coh. cristalline, (ou si X n'est pas f^t lisse sur S) on ne peut [prendre] X̃ comme l'objet final. Mais supposons que l'on puisse trouver une immersion'.
The line under the spectral sequence reads 'généralisant l'isomorphisme donné plus haut'.
